transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Yeah, thanks. Well, I guess what brought me in is... I just can't stop jumping out of my skin. I do maintenance work, and if a breaker snaps loud, or somebody drops a tool, or even if a guy just comes up behind me unannounced, I practically jump out of my boots. 

And it's not just a quick scare, you know? My heart just keeps hammering in my chest long after everyone else has already moved on and gone back to work. I just can't seem to shake it.
Did something traumatic happen to you before all this started?
Yeah. Um... there was an arc-flash accident on this retrofit job I was working on. That's when all this started. It's been going on since that happened, so... about a year and a month now.
Since that accident, have you had unwanted memories of it suddenly pop into your mind?

Yeah, all the time. It's like... out of nowhere, I'll just see that bright flash right in my head. Or I'll hear the new guy yelling. It doesn't even matter what I'm doing. I could just be loading up my tools in the back of the truck, and boom, it just pops up. It knocks me sideways, man. It honestly feels like I'm right back there and it's happening all over again.
Since the accident, have you been going out of your way to avoid reminders of what happened?

Yeah, I do. I mean, I make excuses not to go near certain panels or breakers now. If a job site looks too much like that one, I'll try to get out of it. And I definitely don't want to talk about that day. If I even get close to thinking about it or talking about it, it just starts up in my head and I can't shut it off. So I just try to stay away from anything that reminds me of it.
Since the accident, have you been feeling persistently detached or cut off from other people?
No, I don't think so. I mean, I still talk to my family and the guys on the crew just fine. I don't really feel disconnected from them or anything like that.
Since the accident, have you been blaming yourself or someone else for what happened?
No, not really. I mean, it was an accident. The new guy made a mistake, but I don't sit around blaming him for it. And I don't really blame myself either. It just... it just happened.
Since the accident, have you been feeling persistently afraid, horrified, angry, guilty, or ashamed?

Yeah, I do. I just... I walk around mad all the time now. And guilty, too. It's like I failed that kid, you know? Since I was the experienced guy on the job. And it feels like everybody can see it on me, like they know. So yeah, I just feel angry and guilty pretty much all the time.
